definitions.explanation: A thick, padded hood that covers the head and shoulders, worn to protect against falling objects and sparks during an earthquake or fire. Japanese schoolchildren keep one at their desks, often as a seat cushion, and put it on during evacuation drills.

examples.japanese: {防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧。
examples.english: To put on a disaster hood.

examples.japanese: ⟦{椅子|いす}→椅子：00706_isu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{敷|し}いている→敷く：00366_shiku⟧。
examples.english: The disaster hood is laid on the chair as a cushion.

examples.japanese: ⟦{避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}→避難訓練：28230_hinankunren⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶって→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧⟦{校庭|こうてい}→校庭：04147_koutei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: In the evacuation drill, the children put on their disaster hoods and went out to the schoolyard.

notes:
Built from ⟦{防災|ぼうさい}→防災：07907_bousai⟧ (disaster prevention) and ⟦{頭巾|ずきん}→頭巾：33986_zukin⟧ (hood). Most Japanese adults remember the hood from elementary school, where it hangs on the back of the chair or serves as a cushion until a drill or a real earthquake. Helmets have replaced it in some schools.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧: to put on a disaster hood
- {防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦カバー→カバー：07812_kabaa⟧: a chair cover that holds the hood
- {防災用|ぼうさいよう}⟦ヘルメット→ヘルメット：11325_herumetto⟧: a disaster helmet (the alternative)
